# Scientific Calculator

> A free scientific calculator that works offline: fractions, trigonometry, logarithms, 142 formulas and 78 constants, a unit converter, a graph, a solver, finance, statistics, matrices and complex numbers, and a history of past calculations, exported as text or CSV. Nothing leaves your browser.

A static web app (no account, no server, no tracking): everything is calculated in the browser. Installable as an app on iOS, Android and desktop. Also available as a Chrome extension.

## Links
- [Calculator](https://raad.dev/calculator/): the app, with options and a guide to every function
- [For schools and organizations](https://raad.dev/calculator/admin): turning features of the Chrome extension off for students, from the Google Admin Console
- [Source code and documentation](https://github.com/raad-altaie/scientific-calculator): README, tests, AGPL-3.0 license

## Facts
- Precision: about 15 significant digits (IEEE 754 doubles), shown to 13.
- Angle units: degrees, radians, gradians. Fraction mode. Fix, Sci and Eng formats.
- Panels: formulas and constants; unit converter (37 kinds, with force, torque, density, frequency, flow rate, momentum, radioactivity, magnetic field, radiation dose, molarity, mass concentration, amount of substance, molecular mass, sequence length, enzyme activity, counts per volume and electrical units: current, voltage, charge, resistance, capacitance, inductance), with days between dates, dates moved on, Unix timestamps and time zones; graph (functions, sliders, roots and crossings, areas, derivatives, equations and inequalities of x and y, polar and parametric curves, recursive and explicit sequences, slope fields with their solutions, best fits); solver (roots of equations in exact form as well, inequalities, turning points, polynomials, linear systems, two curves, integrals, sums to infinity, limits, Taylor series, areas between curves, arc lengths, differential equations, time value of money (N, I/Y, PV, PMT, FV), NPV, IRR and payback, loan payment schedules, mortgages with tax, insurance, PMI and HOA, credit card payoff, savings growth, retirement savings and withdrawals, APR and APY, bond price and yield, depreciation, break-even, inflation, percentage change and markup, salary and hourly pay, tip and bill split, fuel cost of a trip, normal, t, chi-squared, F, binomial, Poisson, geometric, hypergeometric, exponential and uniform distributions, confidence intervals; geometry: triangle solver, shapes, solids, points and lines, circle through three points, polygon area); each card of the solver, numbers, chemistry, physics, statistics tests and dates with an Example, and a graph first in its results where one fits; statistics (mean, median, quartiles, standard deviation, variance, mode, histogram and box plot; pairs with linear, quadratic, cubic, exponential, power, logarithmic and logistic fits, correlation and Spearman's rho; hypothesis tests: one- and two-sample t, paired t, z, one and two proportions, chi-squared goodness of fit and independence, ANOVA, correlation); numbers (matrices up to 10 × 10 with eigenvalues, powers, row reduction, null space, LU and QR, least squares, pasted from a spreadsheet or as [1 2; 3 4], an example on each card; vectors; complex numbers in polar and exponential form, polynomials of them, AC impedance of R, L and C; bases and bits up to 128 with byte order, Gray code, truth tables of up to 8 variables minimised (sum of products, product of sums, Karnaugh map), any base from 2 to 36, text and Unicode codes, Base32, Base58, Base64 and Base85, hashes (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512, CRC-32), UUIDs (version 4 and 7, and read), IPv4 and IPv6 subnets (CIDR), IEEE 754; prime factors, GCD and LCM, modular arithmetic, the Chinese remainder theorem, exact big numbers, primes, fractions and repeating decimals).; chemistry (the periodic table of 118 elements with the absorption and emission spectra of 98 of them, from NIST, molar mass, balancing reactions, composition, and more chemistry tools); physics (electronics: resistor colour code, SMD codes and EIA-96, series and parallel networks, Ohm's law, wire resistance and AWG, voltage dividers and Thévenin equivalents, Wheatstone bridges, LED resistors, capacitors, RC and RL circuits, RC, RL and RLC filters (low, high, band, stop), parallel plates, transformers, RMS and LC resonance, three-phase power, RLC impedance, phase, Q and bandwidth, electricity cost, battery life, diodes (Shockley), rectifiers and ripple, BJT switching and bias, MOSFETs, Zener regulators, LM317 regulators, op-amps, 555 timers, dBm, dBV and dBµV levels and gains in dB, E12 values; motion: SUVAT, projectiles, relative velocity and river crossings, circular motion, orbits (Kepler's third law, vis-viva), the rocket equation, pendulums and springs, rotation and moments of inertia, centre of mass; forces: F = ma, inclined planes, Atwood machines and pulleys, collisions, impulse, energy, work, torque and levers, gravitation and the Schwarzschild radius, drag and terminal velocity, Coulomb's law, magnetic force, magnetic fields of wires, solenoids and loops, electromagnetic induction; waves: standing waves, beats, lenses and mirrors, the lensmaker's equation, refraction, interference (double slit, diffraction grating), single-slit diffraction and the Rayleigh criterion, polarisation (Malus, Brewster), Doppler effect of sound and relativistic redshift, photons, decibels; matter: specific and latent heat, mixing, thermal expansion, conduction, radiation, Newton's law of cooling, dew point and humidity, kinetic theory of gases, isothermal, isobaric, isochoric and adiabatic processes, heat engines and Carnot efficiency, stress, strain and Young's modulus, density, pressure, buoyancy, pipe flow, Reynolds number and Darcy friction (Colebrook), Stokes' law; modern and quantum: E = mc², nuclear binding energy, Q-values, photoelectric effect, de Broglie wavelength, uncertainty principle, particle in a box, Compton scattering, quantum tunnelling, special relativity, hydrogen spectrum and Bohr model, radioactive decay; many cards drawn: graphs, rays, fringes, standing waves, energy levels); biology (genetics: Punnett squares of up to six genes and X-linked crosses, Hardy–Weinberg with its chi-square test, chi-square of a cross, two- and three-point gene mapping, chances of offspring, heritability, epistasis, genetic risk with pedigrees, ABO and Rh blood groups; DNA: sequence stats, GC content, reverse complement, translation in six frames and ORFs, the codon wheel, primer Tm by nearest neighbours, A260 concentration and purity, mass, moles and copies, ligation, restriction digests with a virtual gel, PCR amplification, global and local alignment with a dot plot, CRISPR guides, IUPAC motif search, mutagenesis and Gibson primers, genome sizes and copies; proteins: mass, pI, extinction coefficient, hydropathy, amino acids and titration curves, protein assays, Michaelis–Menten with inhibitors and Lineweaver–Burk, Hill binding, dose–response IC50 fitting, purification tables; lab: C1V1 = C2V2, serial dilutions, making solutions, haemocytometer counts, doubling time and OD600, CFU/mL, RPM and RCF, PCR master mix, qPCR ΔΔCt and standard curves, mean ± 2 SE, chromatography Rf, microscopy, gel band sizes, transformation efficiency, seeding plates, MOI, radioisotopes, buffers; cells: water potential, tonicity, SA:V, Q10, Fick diffusion, Nernst and Goldman potentials, free energy, cardiac output and blood pressure, respiration and RQ; health: diagnostic tests, relative risk and odds ratios, SIR epidemics and herd immunity, oxygen–haemoglobin curves, Hodgkin–Huxley action potentials, eGFR and clearance, BMI and BMR, drug levels; ecology: exponential and logistic growth, Lotka–Volterra, mark and recapture, Simpson and Shannon diversity, life tables, energy pyramids, primary productivity, selection and genetic drift, Leslie matrices, competition, species–area and rarefaction, UPGMA and neighbour-joining trees, the molecular clock).
